question: A workflow owner wants feedback from a four-week pilot that will genuinely help her improve the arrangement. Which feedback format is most useful for that purpose?
options: A) Logged cases pairing the input given, the output produced, and what the user needed instead.
B) A weekly satisfaction score from each participant, tracked to show the trend across the four weeks.
C) A count of how often each participant used the arrangement during each week of the pilot period.
D) A free-text comment box at the end of the pilot for any observations participants wish to record.
correct_answers: A) Logged cases pairing the input given, the output produced, and what the user needed instead.
explanations: Correct. Improvement needs cases, not impressions. A logged triple of input, output and the required result shows exactly where the arrangement diverged from what was needed, which is the only feedback that can be turned directly into a change.

A satisfaction trend tells the owner whether things are getting better or worse but never why. A falling score gives her no defect to fix, and a rising one may simply reflect participants lowering their expectations.
Usage counts show adoption rather than quality. Heavy use can mean the arrangement is valuable or that people are repeatedly retrying it because the first result was unusable.

An end-of-pilot comment box collects thoughts long after the events that prompted them, so the detail has faded. It also mixes design feedback with unrelated grumbles and offers no link to specific outputs.
